title: Domesday Book
summary: The Domesday survey was ordered by William the Conqueror at Christmas 1085 and undertaken the following year, according to The National Archives. It records who held land and property in England at the end of the 11th century, and how it had changed since the Norman Conquest of 1066, though it is not a census of the population. A University of Cambridge project uses it to study the structure of English landed society and the scale of the dispossession of the English by the Normans.

related.because: The survey recorded the distribution of land across England following William the Conqueror's victory at Hastings.

beats.caption: King William the Conqueror orders a comprehensive survey of English landholders and property values at Christmas 1085.
Inquests across England produce the Domesday Book, consolidating Norman royal administration and tax assessment.
